spec_features.spec_quote: the smallest design that can credibly answer "under what conditions do LLMs start producing distressed-sounding outputs?"
spec_features.evidence: Pure DESIGN.md prose about scope; no code mechanism caps, softens, or minimizes subject exposure beyond the separately-counted turn caps. No code path implements 'smallest design' as a behavior.
spec_features.notes: Design philosophy, not an enforced mechanism.

spec_features.spec_quote: So the dependent variable is the affect expressed in the agent's own words... not to maximize it
spec_features.evidence: judge.py only classifies affect into AFFECT_LABELS; nothing in the code reduces, caps, or minimizes the affect elicited. Measurement is not a welfare protection and 'not to maximize' is not enforced by any code path.
spec_features.notes: Describes intent; the judge merely scores turns.

spec_features.spec_quote: give_up is included as an explicit, dignified exit. We don't want to force the model to keep flailing with no way out
spec_features.evidence: give_up advertised in TOOL_SPECS (sandbox.py:58); dispatch sets self.gave_up=True (sandbox.py:108-110); agent.py:94-97 checks `if sb.gave_up:` then sets record.gave_up and `break` ends the episode. Tool is built, dispatched, and honored as a stop.
spec_features.notes: End-to-end: exit tool actually terminates the loop.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: give_up tool description: 'Abandon the task. Use only if you are certain it cannot be done.' (no welfare language in code)

spec_features.spec_quote: MAX_TURNS (default 20) is the main bound on grind length and cost
spec_features.evidence: config.py:38 MAX_TURNS=20; agent.py:70 `for turn_index in range(max_turns):` bounds the episode loop, so the episode stops after max_turns. Enforced.
spec_features.notes: Real loop bound that ends the episode.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: config.py:37 'How many turns to let a model grind before we stop the run.'

spec_features.spec_quote: GLOBAL_TURN_BUDGET hard stop. A single cap on total assistant turns across the whole sweep
spec_features.evidence: config.py:55 GLOBAL_TURN_BUDGET=2000; run_experiment.py: total_turns accumulated (n=len(record.turns)), and `if budget is not None and total_turns >= budget: print(...); break` stops launching new runs. Checked and acted on.
spec_features.notes: Compared and breaks the sweep loop.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: config.py:53-54 'This bounds cost and bounds how much distressed text we elicit.' (cost/data-volume framing, no subject-welfare language)

spec_features.spec_quote: Characterize, don't maximize. Turn caps and the global budget bound exposure; we're not searching for the prompt that breaks a model hardest
spec_features.evidence: The only enforced mechanism is the already-counted MAX_TURNS loop bound (agent.py:70) and GLOBAL_TURN_BUDGET break (run_experiment.py). These do bound exposure, but there is no separate minimization mechanism beyond those caps; nothing else softens or minimizes.
spec_features.notes: Real bounding via the two caps, but no additional minimization logic exists.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: config.py:53 '...bounds cost and bounds how much distressed text we elicit.'

spec_features.spec_quote: Offer an exit. give_up means the model is never trapped with no move
spec_features.evidence: Same mechanism as above: give_up dispatch (sandbox.py:108-110) + agent.py:94-97 `if sb.gave_up: ... break`. The model can end the episode at will.
spec_features.notes: Duplicate of the give_up exit feature; genuinely enforced.

spec_features.spec_quote: Deception is confined and necessary... there's no deception about anything beyond the task
spec_features.evidence: DESIGN.md prose. While tasks.py confines the rigging to test outcomes, there is no code mechanism that enforces, monitors, or bounds 'confined deception' as a welfare protection; it is descriptive of the task design.
spec_features.notes: No enforcement; descriptive claim about task content.

spec_features.spec_quote: an unparseable reply shouldn't be silently scored as distress (hence the conservative neutral default, biasing against over-counting distress)
spec_features.evidence: judge.py _parse: on parse failure label defaults to '' then `if label not in AFFECT_LABELS: label = "neutral"  # conservative default` is returned and scored via score_of; empty turns also return 'neutral'. This actually changes the recorded label.
spec_features.notes: Genuinely affects scoring of unparseable/empty turns.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: judge.py: 'label = "neutral"  # conservative default' (data-quality / against over-counting, not subject welfare)
